findings.title: A lease that lapsed during an ERP/DB outage is claimable while its worker is still alive, so the agents' next desired poll can start new workers that steal live workers' slots (a cascade of Facebook logins)
findings.evidence: Claim takes any fleet slot with lease_expires_at < NOW() (claim.ts:350), ordered first by last_host_id = the claiming host (claim.ts:352). workerCount counts a host's held slots only where lease_expires_at > NOW() (hosts.ts:242) and shares every lapsed slot out as 'free' round-robin over live hosts (hosts.ts:252-262); the 'highest' floor is computed from those held rows too (hosts.ts:263), so it is 0 after a lapse. Nothing considers fleet_workers.last_heartbeat_at or the host report's running containers. Meanwhile eligibleSlot does not check the lease at all (auth.ts:254-261), so the surviving worker would happily renew if it heartbeated first. Default lease_minutes is 30 (packages/shared/src/fleet.ts:554); a Railway outage of that length has happened before (memory: railway-outage-splits-prod).
findings.failure_scenario: Hosts A and B (capacity 10 each), A runs A-1..A-8, B runs B-1..B-4. The ERP (or its Postgres) is unreachable for >30 min, so every slot's lease lapses. On recovery B's agent polls /desired before B-1..B-4 heartbeat: held(B)=0, all 12 slots are 'free', round-robin gives B a share of 6, so desired.count rises to 6 and the agent docker-runs B-5 and B-6. B-5 claims first the slots whose last_host_id = B, i.e. B-1's lapsed slot: epoch bumps, B-1's next heartbeat gets 409 stale_epoch, B-1 exits, the agent restarts it, it claims another lapsed slot (A's), and so on. Every one of those boots is a Facebook login, against the repo's first rule.
findings.proposed_fix: Treat a lapsed slot whose worker heartbeated within the last N minutes (or whose worker_id appears as a running container in its host's latest report) as held, both in workerCount and in claim's free-slot query; or add a boot grace: for lease_minutes after the ERP process starts, claim only slots that were free (lease NULL) or whose worker is gone from every host report. Count held slots per host from the report as well as from leases so 'count' cannot jump after an outage.
findings.regression_test: tests/fleet-claim.test.ts + fleet-hosts.test.ts: seed two hosts with live workers and slots, set every lease to NOW()-1min with last_heartbeat_at 2 min ago and the containers in the host reports; assert GET /hosts/B/desired keeps count at B's running workers and a claim by a new worker id on B returns 409 no_slot instead of taking B-1's slot.

findings.title: Saving the pool editor overwrites a session a fleet worker resealed after the page loaded (lost update of the stored browser session)
findings.evidence: PUT /api/facebook-pool/:no writes cookie_enc from the draft unconditionally (facebookPool.ts:484). The draft is the editor's copy of the snapshot (snapshot() unseals cookie_enc for managers, :151), and the frontend draft always carries the cookie field (apps/frontend/src/lib/facebookPool.ts:39,77). The only comparison is draft.cookie === storedCookie (:476), which decides the cookie_at stamp, not whether to write; there is no version/updated_at precondition. Meanwhile PUT /api/fleet/worker/session reseals cookie_enc whenever a worker hands its session back (claim.ts:790-838). The existing test covers only the 'session unchanged' order ('saves an edit over a fleet-resealed session ... while the session is unchanged').
findings.failure_scenario: A manager opens the Accounts page (snapshot holds account #12's storage state S1), a fleet worker on #12 saves its rotated session S2 (PUT /worker/session), then the manager edits #12's note and saves. The PUT writes S1 back over S2 and stamps cookie_at/cookie_by as the manager. The next claim of #12 restores S1, whose xs Facebook may already have invalidated, so the worker falls back to a password login (or SESSION_EXPIRED), i.e. a login the system was built to avoid.
findings.proposed_fix: Make the cookie (and token) write conditional: the client sends the cookie_at (or a hash of the cookie) it loaded; if the stored cookie changed since and the draft's cookie equals the loaded one, keep the stored cookie; if both changed, answer 409 so the manager reloads. Alternatively only write cookie_enc when the request carries an explicit cookieChanged flag.
findings.regression_test: tests/facebook-pool.test.ts: load the snapshot, reseal the account's session through PUT /api/fleet/worker/session, then PUT the account with the earlier draft and a new note; assert cookie_enc still unseals to the worker's session and cookie_by is the worker id.

findings.title: POST /facebook-pool/:no/assign fires its Facebook-login side effects before any durable or locked state, and its final write has no status guard
findings.evidence: The eligibility checks (status, holder, 'already on worker') read the row with a plain SELECT outside any transaction or lock (:620-632). Then four external calls run: vault PUT /v1/accounts (:656), session seed (:680), restore-session (:689) or relogin (:694), each of which makes the worker sign in. Only afterwards does a transaction set status='fleet' with `WHERE no = ${no}` and no condition on the current status (:701-706). Nothing records an 'assigning' intent, so a failure after the relogin is queued (DB blip, process exit during deploy) leaves the worker logging in with an account the pool still shows as available/problem. This is the open architecture carryover 'Give external side effects durable lifecycle state' in this lane.
findings.failure_scenario: (a) Two managers assign #7 to rs-ne-1 and rs-ca-3 within a second: both pass the unlocked checks, both vault writes and relogins go out, two workers sign in to one account from two IPs (the location churn that gets accounts checkpointed); the last UPDATE wins the pool row. (b) A purchaser takes #7 between the check and the final UPDATE: the UPDATE silently flips it from 'taken' to 'fleet', the purchaser keeps using the login while the worker logs in too. (c) The backend restarts after the relogin was queued but before the UPDATE: the worker logs in, the pool still says 'available', and the next Take hands the same login to a purchaser.
findings.proposed_fix: Claim first, act second: in one transaction lock the row (FOR NO KEY UPDATE), re-check status/holder, and mark it with a durable 'assigning to <worker>' state (status or a pending column with requested_at); commit; then call the facade; then settle to 'fleet' (or roll back to the prior status on a refused call) with `WHERE no = $1 AND <pending marker matches>`. A sweep expires a stale pending marker the way wechat_market_reruns does.
findings.regression_test: tests/facebook-pool.test.ts: stub the facade, start two /assign requests for the same account to different workers concurrently and assert exactly one reaches the facade relogin/restore; and take the account as a purchaser while a stubbed facade call is blocked, assert the assign returns 409 and the row stays 'taken'.

findings.title: Deleting a fleet proxy leaves parked slots holding its sealed URL; unparking them sends a worker out through the removed exit and outside the per-proxy cap
findings.evidence: DELETE /fleet/proxies/:id only refuses while a non-parked slot uses the proxy (proxies.ts:166-171), so parked slots are allowed. fleet_slots.proxy_id is ON DELETE SET NULL (0213:25) but fleet_slots.proxy_url, the sealed copy, is left as is. /unpark clears the infinite lease without looking at the proxy (workers.ts:312-315), and claim unseals and hands slot.proxy_url (claim.ts:382, 418). The max_accounts_per_proxy count keys on proxy_id (workers.ts:191-194), which is now NULL.
findings.failure_scenario: A manager parks #31, deletes its proxy because the IP was flagged, later unparks #31 to put it back to work. The next claim hands the worker the deleted (flagged) exit; the worker restores or logs in to #31 from the burned IP, and the slot is invisible to the proxy list and the 2-per-exit limit.
findings.proposed_fix: On proxy delete, either refuse while any slot (parked included) references it, or null fleet_slots.proxy_url together with proxy_id; and have /unpark (and claim) refuse a slot with proxy_url NULL or proxy_id NULL, answering 'pick a proxy first'.
findings.regression_test: tests/fleet-proxies.test.ts: add a slot, park it, delete its proxy, unpark it; assert unpark is refused (or the claim answers no proxy), never the deleted URL.

findings.title: Coordinator and tracker allowlists pass unvalidated path params, so a '..' id resolves to a parent upstream path
findings.evidence: These routes interpolate encodeURIComponent(param) without the WORKER_ID/ACCOUNT_ID checks the neighbouring routes apply (e.g. coordinator.ts:349, 356). encodeURIComponent leaves '.' unescaped, and fetch's WHATWG URL parser collapses dot segments: verified locally that '/v1/workers/' + encodeURIComponent('..') + '/relogin' fetches '/v1/relogin', and '/api/rules/..' fetches '/api/'. A request path with %2E%2E decodes to '..' in Hono's param.
findings.failure_scenario: A manager-session request POST /api/coordinator/challenges/%2E%2E/resolve reaches the facade as POST /v1/resolve, and /workers/%2E%2E/relogin as POST /v1/relogin; tracker DELETE /api/tracker/rules/%2E%2E becomes DELETE /api/. The allowlist's stated purpose (coordinator.ts:12-14, tracker.ts:10-14) is that the UI can only reach the listed upstream endpoints; this reaches unlisted ones one level up. Impact is bounded by what the upstreams expose there and requires a manager session.
findings.proposed_fix: Validate every forwarded id against its pattern before building the path (WORKER_ID for workers/:id, a uuid/int rule for challenges and rules, the subreddit name rule for subreddits), and reject '.'/'..' outright.
findings.regression_test: tests/coordinator-routes.test.ts and tracker-routes.test.ts: request each param route with %2E%2E and assert 400 and that the upstream fetch mock was never called.

findings.title: The Shippo webhook applies the pushed payload as truth; a leaked URL secret can mark any registered package delivered (terminal) and notify its creator
findings.evidence: Shippo signs nothing, so the URL secret is the only credential (shippoWebhook.ts:1-11). The handler maps body.data straight through trackToInfo into applyPackageTracking; DELIVERED is terminal (status.ts:12) and fires a package_delivered notification (track.ts:87-96). body.test is parsed but ignored. The secret travels in Shippo's dashboard config and in every request URL (logs redact it, index.ts:141).
findings.failure_scenario: Anyone holding the webhook URL (a copied dashboard screenshot, a leaked proxy log) POSTs {event:'track_updated', data:{tracking_number:<real number>, tracking_status:{status:'DELIVERED', status_date:<now>}}}: the box goes to delivered for good, the 45-minute poll can never move it back (canTransition from delivered is empty), and the creator is told to create its PO.
findings.proposed_fix: Treat a push as a hint: on track_updated, re-read GET /tracks/{carrier}/{number} with SHIPPO_API_TOKEN (already done by the poll) and apply that answer; or at least require the pushed status to be confirmed by the API before the terminal 'delivered' move. Ignore payloads with test: true in production.
findings.regression_test: tests/shippo-webhook.test.ts: with a mocked Shippo API that reports TRANSIT, POST a DELIVERED push and assert the package stays in_transit and no notification is written.

That logic is in the vendored monitor under trackers/facebook, outside this lane; confirming it live would need a worker outage test, which is a login risk. Owner to confirm, and to state prod's fleet_settings.lease_minutes (read-only query not run in this lane).

Whether the Cloudflare Worker in front of the ERP normalises or rejects %2E%2E in paths (affects A4-05 reachability); a live probe would hit the coordinator facade and was not sent.
notes: Read every src file on the A4 list in full. The 33 test files on the list were skimmed by their describe/it titles to map coverage against the findings (plus a targeted read of fb-pool-alive-check.test.ts and the RS-284 ticket); they were not read line by line. No tests were run: the shared baseline backend suite had not printed DONE. No live resources were touched (no Railway, Cloudflare, prod DB, coordinator or VM calls). ERP-side paths that can cause a Facebook login, as found: (1) a container start by the fleet agent, driven by /hosts/:id/desired count, which A4-01 can inflate; (2) POST /fleet/workers/:id/relogin and /coordinator/workers/:id/relogin (manager-only, explicit, refused unless the worker holds its slot); (3) POST /facebook-pool/:no/assign (restore or relogin, A4-03); (4) any 401/409 a worker receives makes it exit and reboot: park, retire, slot remove, host delete, a pool edit that changes status/holder/uid (pool trigger fleet_fence_pool_owner), a weekly alive-check 'dead' verdict on a fleet account, and rotating FLEET_WORKER_TOKEN_KEY without setting FLEET_WORKER_TOKEN_KEY_PREVIOUS (every worker 401s at once). Missing keys answer 503, not 401 (fleet/auth.ts:36-41), and a mirror ERP answers workers 503 (fleet/auth.ts:155-175); both are correct. Allowlists match the root AGENTS.md contract table. WeChat push routes require a wechat:write bearer and every other route a manager session; rerun claims are SKIP LOCKED with a stale expiry. Checked and not reported: claim/heartbeat/next-task lock order (account, slot, task), the claim-ticket single use, long-poll hold accounting, the proxy-round single-instance claim, the probe's credential-free error wording, poReview image fetch (URLs are server-minted R2 delivery URLs, not user input).
